Subject: Request: privilege matrix + provisioning evidence for SOC 2 SIG

Hi Rachel —

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our vendor SIG/SOC 2 review we need the following artifacts to validate access controls for Redwood's hosted deployment: 

- A current privilege matrix / role list that maps Redwood roles to privileges (console/API/management plane) and which roles are scoped to customer vs Redwood operations.
- Evidence of SCIM provisioning behavior for new user creation and delta syncs (last 30 days). 
- SAML metadata and an example assertion with attributes mapped (email, groups).
- RBAC mapping doc that shows how least-privilege is enforced for service accounts.

If possible, please include a short narrative describing how you enforce least privilege during onboarding and how role changes are audited. We need these artifacts by EOD next Tuesday (2026-05-26) to stay on our compliance timeline.

Also include any notes about retention windows for provisioning logs.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a quick call if needed.

— Mollie
Mollie Santos
Security Program Manager | SafeHarbor Medical

Hi Mollie —

Thanks for the clear list. We can provide everything you asked for. Quick plan below so you know what to expect and when:

2) SCIM evidence: we'll export the last 30 days of delta sync logs and include a short narrative on delta vs full sync behavior (attachment scim_delta_sync_log_20260515.zip).
3) SAML metadata + sample assertion: attaching redwood_saml_metadata.xml and a redacted assertion snippet in the RBAC workbook.
4) Retention: provisioning logs are retained for 90 days by default; we can provide a retention statement and an extended-retention SOW if you need longer.

I expect to send the attachments in two batches today: first-pass artifacts by noon PT, then Laura's audit/narrative and the sync log later this afternoon. If you want us to sign an NDA or a narrow disclosure addendum for any of the docs, let me know.

Also looping Ben to coordinate any contractual follow-ups (PO / mutual action plan).

Cheers,

Mollie / Rachel —

Adding the compliance perspective and a short narrative below. See attached RBAC workbook for examples and a redacted assertion snippet. Highlights: 

- Role taxonomy: we maintain a three-tier role model for platform access (Customer Admin, Customer Operator, Reader) plus internal operational roles (Infra Admin, Support Tech). The privilege_matrix_safeharbor_v1.csv maps each API/console permission to these roles.
- Service accounts: are constrained to scoped tokens and namespaced to customer IDs when operating on customer data. Token issuance is audited and tied to a short-lived key rotation policy.
- Least privilege controls: default-on deny-list for management APIs; just-in-time elevation for troubleshooting via privileged session workflow (requires two-person approval for infra-level elevations).
- Auditing: role changes and elevation events are logged to our immutable audit stream and retained 365 days for SOC 2 purposes; provisioning logs (SCIM) are kept 90 days.

Attachments included: rbac_role_mapping_v2.xlsx (role mappings + redacted SAML assertion), scim_delta_sync_log_20260515.zip (exported delta events in CSV), privilege_matrix_safeharbor_v1.csv.

If you'd like a short write-up that we can drop into your SIG questionnaire, I can produce a 1-page narrative explaining controls and mapping to SIG/SOC 2 criteria by EOD tomorrow.

Laura Bennett
Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference
